options: Building hotels along the whole shore
Dividing a territory into zones with different purposes and rules of use
questions.explain: Functional zoning divides territory into zones with different functions and permitted activities (Topic 8).

questions.q: Which planning tool classifies land from primitive (wild) to urban settings so each area offers a different experience?
questions.explain: ROS classifies settings from primitive to urban (Topic 8).

questions.q: Which are the three zones of a UNESCO biosphere reserve?
questions.explain: Biosphere reserves use the core-buffer-transition model (Topics 8–9).
IUCN Category II is National park (Topic 9).

questions.q: Which is the oldest nature reserve in Central Asia, created in 1926?
questions.explain: Aksu-Zhabagly (1926) is the oldest reserve in Central Asia (Topic 9).

questions.q: Bayanaul National Park (1985) was the first national park of Kazakhstan.
questions.explain: Bayanaul in Pavlodar Region, created in 1985, is the first national park of Kazakhstan (Topic 9).

questions.q: Which UNESCO World Heritage site includes the Korgalzhyn and Naurzum reserves?
options: Saryarka — Steppe and Lakes of Northern Kazakhstan
questions.explain: Korgalzhyn and Naurzum form 'Saryarka — Steppe and Lakes of Northern Kazakhstan' (2008) (Topic 9).

options: Rest in nature in comfortable structures with beds, electricity and service

questions.q: A recreation base (baza otdykha) is best described as...
options: A medical institution with a doctor's programme
A hotel in the city centre
A seasonal or all-year complex with simple accommodation, food and basic leisure
questions.explain: Recreation bases offer simple cottages or rooms, catering and leisure, often by a lake (Topic 10).

questions.q: Transfers, insurance and loyalty discounts belong to which level of a recreational product?
questions.explain: Extra services beyond the main offer form the augmented product (Topic 11).

questions.q: Which principles of a good recreational programme are given in Topic 11?
options: Match the physical abilities of the target group
Maximise the number of visitors regardless of capacity
Use local resources, food and culture
questions.explain: A good programme balances loads, fits the target group, uses local resources and respects carrying capacity (Topic 11).

questions.q: Which document sets the current strategy for Kazakhstan's tourism sector?
options: Global Code of Ethics for Tourism
Law on Specially Protected Natural Areas
Concept for the Development of the Tourism Industry for 2023–2029
questions.explain: The Concept for 2023–2029 was approved by Government Decree No. 262 of 28 March 2023 (Topic 12).

questions.q: Lake Balkhash is fresh in its western part and saline in its eastern part.
questions.explain: Balkhash is half fresh (west) and half saline (east) (Topic 12).

questions.q: Which world recreational region is the largest and the historic centre of '3S' beach tourism?
questions.explain: The Mediterranean is the largest recreational region in the world (Topic 13).

questions.q: Seasonality is a problem only for ski resorts; sanatoriums and lake resorts do not suffer from it.
questions.explain: Lake and beach resorts in Kazakhstan are strongly seasonal; sanatoriums suffer less because treatment does not depend on weather (Topic 14).

questions.q: Fixed costs are 2,000,000, price per guest is 50,000 and variable cost per guest is 30,000. What is the break-even number of guests?
questions.explain: Break-even = fixed costs / (price − variable cost) = 2,000,000 / 20,000 = 100 guests (Topic 14).
